summary: The queue implementation masks runtime failures, leaks file descriptors on oversized logs, triggers unhandled promise rejections in heartbeats, and allows path traversal.

findings.title: runOne reports success on failure
findings.body: In runOne, the catch block returns { id, ok: true } when openJob or handle.write fails. This masks all runtime errors and falsely reports failed jobs as successful to callers.
findings.recommendation: Return { id, ok: false, error } or propagate the error in the catch block.

findings.title: Unclosed file handle leak when log exceeds size limit
findings.body: openJob opens a file handle and registers it in handles before checking stat.size. If stat.size > 1_000_000, an Error is thrown without closing the handle or removing it from the map, leaking file descriptors.
findings.recommendation: Close the file handle with await handle.close() and remove it from handles if the size check fails before throwing the error.

findings.title: Unhandled promise rejection in startHeartbeat interval
findings.body: startHeartbeat calls fs.appendFile inside setInterval without awaiting it or attaching a .catch handler. Any filesystem I/O error will result in an unhandled promise rejection, which can crash the Node.js process.
findings.recommendation: Handle errors from fs.appendFile with .catch() and return the interval timer ID so it can be cleared.

findings.title: Path traversal via unvalidated job ID
findings.body: openJob and startHeartbeat concatenate the id parameter directly into filesystem paths without validation or sanitization. If id contains path traversal sequences such as '../', arbitrary files can be appended to.
findings.recommendation: Validate id using a strict whitelist regex (e.g. /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$/) or sanitize it with path.basename before constructing file paths.

samples.summary: src/queue.js contains error masking in runOne, file handle leaks on oversized logs, unhandled promise rejections in heartbeat intervals, and unvalidated path interpolation.

findings.title: Failure catch block returns ok: true masking job execution errors
findings.body: In runOne, the catch block returns { id, ok: true } instead of reporting failure. Any error during openJob or handle.write is swallowed and incorrectly reported as a successful execution.
findings.recommendation: Return { id, ok: false, error } in the catch block of runOne so callers can detect and handle job failures.

findings.title: File handle leak and stale registry entry when log exceeds size limit
findings.body: In openJob, if stat.size exceeds 1,000,000 bytes, an Error is thrown without closing the open FileHandle or removing the id from handles, leaking file descriptors and retaining stale handles.
findings.recommendation: Close the handle with await handle.close() and remove the key from handles before throwing the error, or defer adding to handles until size validation passes.

findings.title: Unhandled promise rejection and untracked interval in startHeartbeat
findings.body: startHeartbeat calls asynchronous fs.appendFile inside setInterval without handling promise rejections. If write operations fail, Node.js will emit an unhandled promise rejection. Additionally, the interval timer is not returned, preventing cleanup.
findings.recommendation: Handle errors by attaching a .catch() handler to fs.appendFile or using an async error handler, and return the interval ID so callers can cancel it via clearInterval.

findings.title: Path traversal via unvalidated job identifier in filesystem paths
findings.body: The id parameter is interpolated directly into filesystem paths (/var/jobs/${id}.log and /var/jobs/${id}.beat) without validation. Untrusted IDs with path traversal characters (such as ../) allow reading/writing files outside the target directory.
findings.recommendation: Validate id against an allowlist pattern (such as /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$/) or use path.basename before constructing file paths.

samples.summary: The queue implementation masks job failures as successful, risks process crashes from unhandled promise rejections in heartbeats, and leaks file handles on size limit errors.

findings.title: Catch block returns success status on error
findings.body: In runOne, the catch block returns { id, ok: true } when an exception is thrown during openJob or handle.write. This silently masks failures and reports failed jobs as successful to callers.
findings.recommendation: Return { id, ok: false, error } in the catch block or rethrow the error.

findings.title: Unhandled promise rejection in heartbeat interval
findings.body: In startHeartbeat, fs.appendFile returns a Promise from node:fs/promises inside setInterval without error handling. Any filesystem error (such as EACCES or ENOSPC) will cause an unhandled promise rejection and terminate the Node.js process.
findings.recommendation: Attach a .catch() handler or wrap the callback in an async try/catch to handle errors.

findings.title: Unclosed file handle when log size exceeds limit
findings.body: In openJob, if stat.size exceeds 1,000,000, an error is thrown after opening the file and inserting it into handles. The file handle is never closed or removed from handles, resulting in a leaked file descriptor.
findings.recommendation: Close the handle with await handle.close() and remove it from handles before throwing the error.
